reasons: The save and update functions do not catch damaged stored data, while the read function does.
The archive action in the UI permanently deletes, but its label says archive.

terms.meaning: a named description of what fields a piece of data must have
a short URL-friendly name built from words, used in web addresses
a small save area built into the browser

sections.name: InterviewRound
sections.title: Interview round choices
sections.what: Lists the kinds of interview rounds the app recognizes, such as phone screen, case, technical, and final.
sections.why: Fixed choices keep interview records consistent across pages.
sections.watch_out: A new round must also be added to the parsing prompt, or the AI will not return it.

sections.name: Interview
sections.title: One interview record
sections.what: Describes one interview: round, scheduled time, interviewer, format, notes, and outcome.
sections.why: Lets one application hold several interviews.
sections.watch_out: Dates are stored as text, so sorting only works if the formats are consistent.

sections.name: Application
sections.title: One job application record
sections.what: Describes one application: company, role, status, score, the AI scoring result, interviews, contacts, notes, and a saved resume.
sections.why: This is the central record that every page reads and writes.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are loosely typed, so a misspelled field name will not be caught by the editor.

sections.name: TargetBucket
sections.title: Target role bucket shape
sections.what: Describes a target role type with its names, title keywords, preferred sectors, locations, companies, seniority levels, and a weight.
sections.why: Lets the user define the roles they want, and the scoring uses that list.
sections.watch_out: The weight is stored here, but this file does not show how it is applied.

sections.name: getApplications
sections.title: Reading all applications
sections.what: Returns every saved application and adds how many days ago it was captured.
sections.why: The day count powers the age labels on the pipeline.
sections.watch_out: Damaged stored data returns an empty list with no warning, so the user may think every application is gone.

sections.name: saveApplication
sections.title: Adding or replacing an application
sections.what: Adds a new application, or replaces the one with the same id, then tells open screens to refresh.
sections.why: One save function handles both new and edited records.
sections.watch_out: Reading the stored list is not protected here, so damaged data throws an error.

sections.name: getApplication
sections.title: Finding one application by slug
sections.what: Returns the first application whose slug matches.
sections.why: Pages open a record from the slug in the web address.
sections.watch_out: If two applications share a slug, the second one can never be opened.

sections.name: updateApplication
sections.title: Changing some fields of an application
sections.what: Updates selected fields of one application and records the update time.
sections.why: Lets a page change one field without rewriting the whole record.
sections.watch_out: If the id does not exist, nothing happens and no error is shown.

sections.name: deleteApplication
sections.title: Permanently deleting an application
sections.what: Removes one application from storage and tells open screens to refresh.
sections.why: The archive action on the application page calls this.
sections.watch_out: Deletion is permanent. The archive button label is misleading.

sections.name: generateSlug
sections.title: Building a URL slug
sections.what: Builds a lowercase, hyphenated name from the company and role.
sections.why: Gives each application a readable web address.
sections.watch_out: Two applications with the same company and role get the same slug.

sections.name: generateId
sections.title: Creating a random id
sections.what: Creates a short random id for a new application.
sections.why: Gives each record a key that is usually unique.
sections.watch_out: Random ids are not guaranteed unique, and the method used is an older one.

summary: Defines what a job application record looks like and provides the functions that read, add, change, and delete those records in the browser's local storage.
purpose: Holds all job application data for the app, saved per browser.
why: Likely reason: the app stores data in the browser instead of a server, so it needs no database. The code does not state this.
how: Defines types for applications, interviews, and target role buckets. Reads the saved list from local storage, adds a count of days since capture to each item, and writes the full list back after each change. Also builds URL slugs from company and role, and creates random ids.
inputs: Application objects and partial changes from the pages, plus a slug or id to find one record.
outputs: Lists or single applications, and a browser event named careeros-data-change after each write.
risks: Data exists only in this browser. Damaged stored data can make saving throw an error. Deletion is permanent. Slugs can repeat when company and role match, and lookups return the first match. Random ids are short and could clash. Many fields are typed loosely.
debug: If applications vanish, check the local storage key named careeros_apps and confirm you are using the same browser. If saves fail, the stored text may be invalid, and the save functions do not catch that. Inspect the stored text before clearing it.
